1.subtopic: Variation of g with Depth, Altitude, Density, and Latitude
1.solution:
\(g = \dfrac{GM}{R^2}\) and \(M = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3\rho\), so \(g = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi G R\rho\), i.e. \(g \propto R\rho\).
\(\dfrac{g_A}{g_B} = \dfrac{r_1\rho_1}{r_2\rho_2}\).

3.solution:
When the two interfering waves have unequal amplitudes, they cannot cancel completely at the minima.
Hence there is some residual intensity even in the regions of destructive interference.

5.solution:
By conservation of angular momentum, \(\omega_c = \dfrac{I_1\omega_1 + I_2\omega_2}{I_1 + I_2}\).
Rotational KE \(= \dfrac{1}{2}(I_1 + I_2)\omega_c^2 = \dfrac{(I_1\omega_1 + I_2\omega_2)^2}{2(I_1 + I_2)}\).

6.solution:
\(\rho = \dfrac{m}{\pi r^2 L}\), so \(\dfrac{\Delta\rho}{\rho} = \dfrac{\Delta m}{m} + 2\dfrac{\Delta r}{r} + \dfrac{\Delta L}{L}\).
\(= \left(\dfrac{0.003}{0.3} + 2\times\dfrac{0.005}{0.5} + \dfrac{0.06}{6}\right)\times 100 = 1 + 2 + 1 = 4\%\).

7.subtopic: SHM Kinematics — Displacement, Velocity, Phase, and Damping
7.solution:
\(\Delta\phi = \left(\dfrac{2\pi}{T_1} - \dfrac{2\pi}{T_2}\right)t\) with \(T_1 = T,\ T_2 = \tfrac{3T}{2}\), at \(t = 2T\).
\(\Delta\phi = \left(2\pi - \dfrac{4\pi}{3}\right)\dfrac{2T}{T}\)... evaluating per phase accumulated \(= \dfrac{4\pi}{3}\,rad\).

8.solution:
Node analysis (A at \(5\,V\), D at \(0\)) gives nodes B and C at equal potential, so the \(B\)–\(C\) arm carries no current (balanced bridge).
Equivalent resistance \(= 10\,\Omega\), so \(I = \dfrac{5}{10} = 0.5\,A\).

9.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
9.subtopic: Photoelectric Effect — Stopping Potential, Threshold, and Work Function
9.solution:
Transition from third orbit \((n=3)\) to the ground state \((n=1)\):
\(E = 13.6\left(\dfrac{1}{1^2} - \dfrac{1}{3^2}\right) = 13.6\times\dfrac{8}{9} \approx 12.1\,eV\).
\(eV_s = E - \phi_0 = 12.1 - 4.1 = 8\,eV\), so \(V_s \approx 8\,V\).
9.note: Stem says the electron jumps from the THIRD orbit to the GROUND STATE (n=3 to n=1), giving E = 13.6(1 - 1/9) = 12.1 eV and Vs = 12.1 - 4.1 = 8 V (option D). The AK's own solution wrongly used n=2 as the ground state (E = 13.6(1 - 1/4) = 10.2 eV) to get 6 V.

11.chapter: Magnetic Fields Due to Electric Current
11.solution:
Magnetising field at the centre of a long solenoid is \(H = nI\) (independent of the medium).
\(B = \mu_0 n I\) but \(H = \dfrac{B}{\mu_0} = nI\).

12.subtopic: Moment of Inertia, Theorems, and Radius of Gyration
12.solution:
Each mass is at distance \(\dfrac{L}{\sqrt2}\) (half-diagonal) from the centre.
\(I = 4M\left(\dfrac{L}{\sqrt2}\right)^2 = 2ML^2\). With \(I = (4M)k^2\), \(k = \sqrt{\dfrac{2ML^2}{4M}} = \dfrac{L}{\sqrt2}\).

13.subtopic: Single Slit Diffraction and Resolving Power
13.solution:
Width between first minima on either side of the central maximum \(= \dfrac{2\lambda D}{a}\).
\(= \dfrac{2\times 4500\times10^{-10}\times 1.5}{0.3\times10^{-3}} = 4.5\,mm\).

14.solution:
Boy A runs distance \(vt\), boy B runs \(v_1 t\) perpendicular to AB. By Pythagoras: \((vt)^2 = x^2 + (v_1 t)^2\).
\((v^2 - v_1^2)t^2 = x^2 \Rightarrow t = \left(\dfrac{x^2}{v^2 - v_1^2}\right)^{1/2}\).

16.subtopic: Magnetic Moment of Current Loop and Galvanometer Instruments
16.solution:
A wire of length \(L\) bent into a single circular turn has circumference \(L=2\pi r\Rightarrow r=\dfrac{L}{2\pi}\).
Area \(A=\pi r^2=\pi\left(\dfrac{L}{2\pi}\right)^2=\dfrac{L^2}{4\pi}\).
Maximum torque \(\tau_{\max}=BIA=\dfrac{L^2 I B}{4\pi}\) (option B).
The AK keys \(\dfrac{L^2 I B}{2}\), which omits the correct area factor — it is wrong.
16.note: AK key D is wrong. Single-turn coil: r=L/2pi, A=L^2/4pi, tau_max=BIA=L^2 I B/4pi = option B.

17.subtopic: Self-Inductance, Energy Stored, and LR Circuit
17.solution:
The four inductors (2 H, 3 H, 4 H, 6 H) are connected in parallel between A and B.
\(\dfrac{1}{L} = \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{1}{6} = \dfrac{6+4+3+2}{12} = \dfrac{15}{12} = \dfrac{5}{4}\), so \(L = \dfrac{4}{5}\,H\).

18.solution:
Top branch: three capacitors in parallel \(= 3C\). Bottom branch: two capacitors in series \(= \dfrac{C}{2}\).
These two branches are in parallel: \(C_{eq} = 3C + \dfrac{C}{2} = \dfrac{7C}{2}\). Setting \(\dfrac{7C}{2} = 14\,\mu F\) gives \(C = 4\,\mu F\).

20.solution:
Molecular collisions in an ideal gas are perfectly elastic.
Hence both kinetic energy and momentum are conserved.

21.subtopic: Reactance — Inductive, Capacitive, and Single-Element Circuits
21.solution: In a pure inductor the current lags the applied voltage by \(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\) radian.

22.subtopic: First Law, Internal Energy, and Work-Heat Relations
22.solution:
Isothermal \(\Rightarrow \Delta U = 0\). First law: \(\Delta Q = \Delta U + \Delta W = 0 + (-150) = -150\,J\).
Negative \(Q\) means \(150\,J\) of heat is removed from the gas.

23.subtopic: Single Slit Diffraction and Resolving Power
23.solution:
Secondary maxima: \(x_n = \dfrac{(2n+1)\lambda D}{2a}\). 2nd max of \(\lambda\) coincides with 3rd max of \(\lambda_0\):
\(5\lambda = 7\lambda_0 \Rightarrow \lambda_0 = \dfrac{5\times 6384}{7} = 4560\,\text{\AA}\).

25.subtopic: Circular Motion — Angular Velocity, Centripetal Force, Vertical Circle
25.solution:
At top A (start), \(v_A = 0\) so \(a_A = 0\). Energy from A to side C (drop \(= l\)): \(\tfrac12 mv_C^2 = mgl \Rightarrow v_C^2 = 2gl\).
\(a_C = \dfrac{v_C^2}{l} = 2g\). Increase in centripetal acceleration \(= 2g - 0 = 2g\).

26.subtopic: Radiation — Stefan, Wien, Newton's Law of Cooling, Black Body
26.solution:
Newton's law of cooling: \(\dfrac{\theta_1-\theta_2}{t} = K\left(\dfrac{\theta_1+\theta_2}{2}-\theta_0\right)\).
Stage 1: \(\dfrac{30}{5} = K(45)\). Stage 2: \(\dfrac{20}{t} = K(20)\). Dividing gives \(t = 7.5\,min\).
Total time \(= 5 + 7.5 = 12.5\,min\).

27.subtopic: Faraday's and Lenz's Laws — Induced EMF, Current, and Charge
27.solution:
Square lies in the x–y plane, so \(\vec A = L^2\hat k\).
\(\phi = \vec B\cdot\vec A = B_0(2\hat i + 3\hat j + 4\hat k)\cdot L^2\hat k = 4B_0 L^2\,Wb\).

28.solution:
Right-angle vertex Q, the two \(-2q\) at distance \(l\) (legs), and \(-2q\)–\(-2q\) separated by \(l\sqrt2\) (hypotenuse).
\(U = -\dfrac{2kQq}{l} - \dfrac{2kQq}{l} + \dfrac{4kq^2}{l\sqrt2} = 0 \Rightarrow Q = \dfrac{q}{\sqrt2}\).

29.subtopic: Surface Tension, Surface Energy, and Capillary Rise
29.solution:
Area \(\propto r^2\): \(4a\) means radius doubles \((r_2 = 2r_1)\). Capillary rise \(h \propto \dfrac{1}{r}\).
\(h_2 = \dfrac{r_1}{r_2}h = \dfrac{h}{2}\).

30.solution:
Small body in a watch glass: \(T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{R}{g}}\).
\(= 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{1.6}{10}} = 2\pi(0.4) = 0.8\pi\,s\).

31.solution: The Ex-OR gate outputs '1' only when an odd number of its inputs are '1'.

32.chapter: Magnetic Fields Due to Electric Current
32.solution:
Inside (\(x = r/2\)): \(B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I x}{2\pi r^2} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r}\). Outside (\(x = 3r\)): \(B_1 = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi(3r)} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{6\pi r}\).
\(\dfrac{B}{B_1} = \dfrac{1/4}{1/6} = \dfrac{6}{4} = \dfrac{3}{2}\).

33.subtopic: Doppler Effect — Moving Source and Observer
33.solution:
Source moving towards stationary observer: \(n = n_0\dfrac{v}{v - v_s}\) with \(v_s = \dfrac{v}{10}\).
\(\dfrac{n}{n_0} = \dfrac{v}{v - v/10} = \dfrac{10}{9}\).

34.subtopic: Viscosity, Stokes' Law, Terminal Velocity, and Reynolds
34.solution:
At terminal velocity, net force = 0: \(F + U = mg\), where upthrust \(U = \dfrac{m}{d_1}d_2 g = mg\dfrac{d_2}{d_1}\).
\(F = mg - mg\dfrac{d_2}{d_1} = mg\left(1 - \dfrac{d_2}{d_1}\right)\).

35.subtopic: Pipes, Resonance Tube, and Doppler Effect
35.solution:
Closed pipe fundamental \(n = \dfrac{v}{4L} = 400\,Hz\). Filling 1/3 with water leaves air column \(\dfrac{2L}{3}\).
New fundamental \(n' = \dfrac{v}{4(2L/3)} = \dfrac{3}{2}\times 400 = 600\,Hz\). Next allowed mode (3rd harmonic) \(= 3\times 600 = 1800\,Hz\).

36.solution:
The circuit is (A NOR B) AND C, i.e. \(Y = \overline{(A+B)}\cdot C\).
\(Y = 1\) only when \(A = 0, B = 0, C = 1\). So for \(Y = 0\) the inputs must NOT be \((0,0,1)\).

37.subtopic: SHM Kinematics — Displacement, Velocity, Phase, and Damping
37.solution:
\(v = \dfrac{dx}{dt} = -A\omega\sin(\omega t + \tfrac{\pi}{6})\); maximum when \(\omega t + \tfrac{\pi}{6} = \tfrac{\pi}{2}\).
\(\omega t = \tfrac{\pi}{3} \Rightarrow t = \dfrac{\pi}{3\omega}\,s\).

38.subtopic: Power in AC Circuit — Average, Factor, Wattless
38.solution:
CR circuit, \(\cos\phi = \dfrac{R}{\sqrt{R^2 + X_C^2}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\Rightarrow X_C = R\). Halving \(f\) doubles \(X_C\): \(X_C' = 2R\).
\(\cos\phi' = \dfrac{R}{\sqrt{R^2 + 4R^2}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt5}\).

39.solution:
Convex mirror \(f = \dfrac{R}{2} = 10\,m\). Mirror formula gives object distances \(u_1 = 50\,m\) (image \(25/3\)) and \(u_2 = 25\,m\) (image \(50/7\)).
Speed \(= \dfrac{50-25}{30} = \dfrac{5}{6}\,m/s = 3\,km/hr\).

40.subtopic: Gas Laws and Ideal Gas Equation
40.solution: Boyle's law: \(P_2 = \dfrac{P_1}{1.07} = 0.9346 P_1\)... for the pressure to drop. For volume increase of 7% at constant T the pressure decreases; the required percentage change in magnitude \(= \dfrac{0.07}{1.07}\times 100 \approx 6.5\%\).

41.solution:
Sonometer with hanging weight: \(n = \dfrac{1}{2l}\sqrt{\dfrac{Mg}{m}}\), so \(\dfrac{l_2}{l_1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{g_2}{g_1}}\).
At the equator \(g\) is smaller \((g_2 < g_1)\), so \(l_2 < l_1\): the vibrating length should be decreased.

45.subtopic: Series LCR — Impedance, Phase, and Resonance
45.solution:
Removing L gives \(\tan(\pi/3) = \dfrac{X_C}{R}\); removing C gives \(\tan(\pi/3) = \dfrac{X_L}{R}\). Hence \(X_L = X_C\).
With both present \(Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2} = R\), so \(\cos\phi = \dfrac{R}{Z} = 1\) (resonance).

47.subtopic: p-n Junction Diode — Biasing, I-V, and Rectifiers
47.solution:
A diode is reverse biased when its p-side (anode) is at a lower potential than its n-side (cathode).
In figure (B), the resistor connects \(-5\,V\) to the anode and the cathode goes to \(+3\,V\): anode \(<\) cathode, so it is reverse biased. The option text '(B)' corresponds to choice C.

Under natural relabel (image order = A,B,C,D), the reverse-biased circuit is figure B (anode at -5V, cathode at +3V => Vanode<Vcathode). AK keyed option text pointed to figure B. Answer = B.

Beat frequency \(= 258 - 256 = 2\,Hz\).
Time between two consecutive maxima \(= \dfrac{1}{2} = 0.5\,s\).
